title: Restrict the Notifications API to secure contexts
body:
Chromium is moving to [restrict access to the notifications API over insecure contexts](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/forum/#!topic/Blink-dev/IVgkxkRNtMo). There will be a deprecation warning in M58, scheduled for April 2017, with full removal in M60, scheduled for August 2017. The proposed behaviour is that calls to Notification.requestPermission() and the Notification constructor from an insecure context will act as though the user has denied permission (similar to the behaviour of the geolocation API from an insecure context).

Motivations for the restriction are as follows:

 * The notification permission acceptance rate for HTTPS sites is 3x greater than for HTTP sites in Chrome
 * Over 90% of daily notification permission requests in Chrome are already made from a secure context
 * Notifications are overwhelming produced in tandem with the Push API which is [already restricted to secure contexts](https://w3c.github.io/push-api/#security-and-privacy-considerations). This restriction is only relevant for sites displaying local notifications while they are open in a browser tab
 * Aligning with the requirements of the Push API reduces developer friction and improves platform predictability
 * Chromium already requires local notifications on Android to be requested over a secure context
 * Notifications allow access to privileged system UI, making them a powerful feature

In light of this, we'd like to propose an update to the spec to explicitly require that user agents only make the Notifications API available over secure contexts, and to codify the behaviour of the API when requested from an insecure context. We also welcome suggestions on our proposed behaviour and whether it could be improved.
